Guide

What does a landscape renovation cost in Baton Rouge?

Every renovation is scoped to the property. Here is what moves the scope up or down.

How big a project is it

A landscape renovation can be a small, single-bed refresh or a full reset of every bed across the front of a house. A large property, extensive removal, or premium plant material makes it a bigger job. The only firm number comes from a look at the property, which is free.

What drives the scope

A renovation comes down to a handful of things:

  • Bed square footage. More bed area means more prep, plants and mulch.
  • Plant size at install. Larger, more mature plants cost more but read as finished sooner.
  • Removal volume. Tearing out overgrown shrubs and hauling them off is real labor.
  • Access. A backyard a machine cannot reach costs more than an open front bed.
  • Whether irrigation is present. Existing beds and irrigation change the scope.

Why bed lines matter more than plant count

It is tempting to judge a renovation by how many plants go in. In practice, the shape of the beds and the crispness of the edging do more for how a house looks from the street than sheer plant count. A renovation resets the bones, the bed lines, the edging, the soil, not just the greenery, which is why a well-designed bed with fewer, better-placed plants often out-performs a crowded one.

Where the value is

What a renovation buys is a job planned properly, built with good material, and finished so it still looks right in a few years. You get a written scope and estimate before anything starts, so there are no surprises.

Common questions

How long does a renovation take?
Most residential front-bed renovations are completed in one to three days once scheduled.
Do you remove the old plants?
Yes, demolition and removal of tired plant material is part of the written scope.
